svg.text: Nine members across four architecture families. The champion is a weighted arithmetic mean of the members’ test probabilities, weights renormalized to sum to 1.
INPUT 96×96×3 H&E patch, raw [0,255] · OUTPUT one tumour probability · METRIC AUROC · public 0.9660 / private 0.9587 · SOURCE research:histopath_pcam, appendix

text.tspan: candidates dragged the blend and were cut
promotion decided only by the hidden set;

svg.text: the honest baseline the whole campaign is measured against
the mirage lineage: weakest solo, best teammate
lean VGG trained from random init, widths 24 / 48 / 96
~250K params — small capacity mirages less and diversifies more
members 3–5 are one recipe at three seeds, Σ 0.32
GroupPool head; weight decay + hard short epoch cap
heaviest single weight in the blend
a different framework, not a different symmetry — that is what decorrelated
steerable escnn: flipRot2dOnR2(N=4) = D4, regular_repr, GroupPooling head
blocks of R2Conv + InnerBN + ReLU + antialiased avgpool, widths 8/16/32/48
agent-promoted as part of the 3-seed average — private 0.9587
the loop stopped here: its next three candidates were rejected, not fitted
member chosen autonomously by the agent

text.tspan: The blend is deliberately unbalanced toward
equivariance (0.76 of the budget across families
3 and 4) because built-in D4 symmetry was the
only thing that improved the hidden-set score
The two non-equivariant members are kept not
for strength but for disagreement: they fail on
different patches than the other seven.

svg.text: Four families by blend budget: pretrained CNN 0.12 · from-scratch CNN 0.12 · p4m group-equivariant 0.56 · steerable e2cnn 0.20. What an ensemble wants is not a better member but a decorrelated one.
